title: The Silent Crash
narration: September 1959. A metal sphere slams into the Moon at over 10,000 kilometers per hour. No explosion. No sound. Just silence. [gasp] That was Luna 2, the first human object to touch another world. But why did it go silent, and what did it leave behind?
visual_goal: A dramatic, silent lunar impact viewed from space; a small probe hitting the grey regolith, kicking up dust in an eerie vacuum.

title: A Giant Leap for Mankind
narration: Ten years later, humans followed. Apollo 11 launched and reached lunar orbit in 76 hours. Then, on July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong took that first step. Just twelve people have ever walked on that dusty surface.
visual_goal: Iconic footage-style animation of Apollo 11 launch, Earth receding, and the first footprint in the regolith.

title: The Silent Sentry
narration: It's been Earth's silent companion for 4.5 billion years. It orbits us at an average distance of 384,400 kilometers, its gravity gently tugging our tides. But what if it wasn't always there?
visual_goal: A time-lapse of the Moon orbiting Earth, with tidal bulges visible on the oceans; transition to a starry nebula.

title: Born from Chaos
narration: We didn't know its origin until we brought back 382 kilograms of lunar rock. Those Apollo samples revealed a violent birth: a Mars-sized body smashed into early Earth, and the debris coalesced to form our Moon.
visual_goal: A stylized animation of the giant-impact hypothesis: two protoplanets colliding in space, a ring of debris forming the Moon.

title: A Frozen Face
narration: Look at its face—it never changes. The Moon rotates once every 27.32 days, exactly matching its orbit around us. That's why we always see the same side. A fixed, silent stare from a world locked in time.
visual_goal: A rotating Moon animation showing the near side always facing the camera, with the far side briefly shown as a dark mystery.

title: Extreme Silence
narration: That stare hides brutal extremes. At the equator, daytime heat soars, but lunar night plunges to -173 degrees Celsius. A silent, frozen desert with no air, no wind, and no sound.
visual_goal: Split-screen visual of a scorching lunar day with a blazing sun, slowly fading into an inky, frozen night with sharp stars.

title: A Lighter Step
narration: But here, you'd feel light. The Moon's gravity is just 0.1654 times Earth's. A 100-kilogram person would weigh only 16.5 kilos. You could leap six times higher, and to escape its pull, you'd only need to reach 2.38 kilometers per second.
visual_goal: Astronauts bounding across the lunar surface in slow motion, showing high jumps and floating dust, against a backdrop of Earth.

title: A Heavy Heart
narration: Mass is stubborn. The Moon holds 7.342 times 10 to the 22 kilograms of rock. Its radius stretches 1,737.4 kilometers. But despite its bulk, its silence is deafening—a world with no atmosphere to carry a cry.
visual_goal: An artistic representation of the Moon's immense mass: a cross-section showing its layers, surrounded by a silent, airless void.

title: The Fragile Link
narration: After 1969, we went back five more times. But no human has set foot there since 1972. [whisper] We left footprints and silence, but we brought back a piece of its 4.5-billion-year story. That's all we have.
visual_goal: A montage of the Apollo landing sites, now still & abandoned, ending with a single, clear footprint in the regolith.

title: The Answer in the Dust
narration: So why did Luna 2 go quiet? Because the Moon has no air to carry sound, and no wind to stir its dust. It's a silent archive. The only voice is our own. [gasp] The story of Earth is written in that silence—if we dare to read it.
visual_goal: A final shot of the lunar surface, with Earth rising in the background, emphasizing the desolate silence and the hint of our planet's story.
